**Area:** [Web, network & communication](../COVERAGE.md#web) · **Apple:** [Network](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/network) · **Issues:** [`area:web`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Aweb)

## How isim implements it

- **Passthrough:** host sockets, with the host's OpenSSL for TLS and isim's own mDNS. QUIC is a stub (the host's OpenSSL 3.0 has no QUIC).
- **Adapted:** reports measure what isim's sockets see; application services are Bonjour services of the app's own type; privacy contexts and proxies are kept with the parameters.

## API

| API / feature | Status | iOS | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Network framework `NWPathMonitor` (`pathUpdateHandler`, `currentPath`, `for await`) | ✅ | ≤17 | mirrors the host's connectivity (Wi-Fi/Ethernet), polled every 2 s; tested |
| Network framework `NWConnection`, `NWListener`, `NWEndpoint`, `NWParameters` (TCP, UDP) | ✅ | ≤17 | host sockets; states (`waiting` on refused/DNS failure), send/receive/receiveMessage, final messages, `currentPath` endpoints, UDP listener connections, TCP options. Tested (HelloConnections) |
| Network framework TLS (`NWProtocolTLS`, `sec_protocol_options` verify block, ALPN, TLS listeners, client certificates, DTLS) | ✅ | ≤17 | the host's OpenSSL: clients check the host's CA store and the host name, or the app's verify block decides with the peer's chain in `sec_trust_t` (`sec_trust_copy_ref`: a SecTrust with the SSL policy, for evaluation or pinning); ALPN, minimum/maximum version, negotiated version/ALPN metadata, `sec_protocol_metadata_access_peer_certificate_chain`; TLS listeners with a server identity (`sec_identity_create`, `sec_protocol_options_set_local_identity`), client certificates (challenge block, required by the server's verify block); DTLS 1.2 over UDP (connections and listeners). Tested (swift-network) |
| Network framework QUIC (`NWProtocolQUIC` options and metadata with Apple's members, `ApplicationError`, `KeepAliveBehavior`, `NWParameters(quic:)`, `.quic(alpn:)`, `.quicDatagram(alpn:)`, `NWMultiplexGroup`; the iOS 26 `QUIC`, `QUIC.TLS`, `QUIC.Stream`, `QUIC.Datagrams`, `QUICStream`, `QUICDatagram` and `NetworkConnection<QUIC>`'s streams, datagrams and properties) | 🧩 | ≤17 | stub: the types are Apple's so apps compile, but connections and multiplex groups fail with `ENOTSUP` and opening streams or datagrams throws it (isim has no QUIC transport yet: issue #851 part 2). | Network framework Bonjour (`NWListener.service`, `NWBrowser`, `.service` endpoints, TXT records) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: apps of this isim device find each other at once in a local registry (`$ISIM_DATA/Library/isim/Bonjour`), and services are advertised and browsed over multicast DNS on the host's network (PTR/SRV/TXT/A, announcements and goodbyes, legacy unicast queries; one responder per app, sharing port 5353 with the host's), so other machines and isim devices see them; `.service` endpoints resolve over mDNS. No name probing (a name already seen gets " (2)"). `ISIM_MDNS=0`: the local registry only. Tested (test_connections, test_connections_mdns against a Python mDNS peer) |
| Network framework `NWProtocolWebSocket`, `NWProtocolFramer`, `NWConnectionGroup` | ✅ | ≤17 | WebSocket client and server (handshake with additional headers / subprotocols / client request handler, text/binary/ping/pong/close messages, auto-reply ping, metadata); custom framers (`NWProtocolFramerImplementation`: start with a handshake, `parseInput`/`deliverInput`, `handleOutput`/`writeOutput`, `markReady`, message metadata) over TCP or TLS; `NWConnectionGroup` with `NWMulticastGroup` (UDP multicast: join, receive with the sender, send to the group or one member, reply, `extract`). Tested (swift-network NWProtocols) |
| `NWConnection` establishment and data transfer reports (`requestEstablishmentReport`, `EstablishmentReport` with resolutions and handshakes, `startDataTransferReport`, `PendingDataTransferReport.collect`, `DataTransferReport` / `PathReport`), `receiveDiscontiguous`, `receiveMessageDiscontiguous`, `NWConnection(from:to:using:)`, `NWConnection(message:)`; `NetworkChannel.establishmentReport()` / `dataTransferReport()` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: isim measures what its sockets see. A resolution is the host resolver's query (its time and address count), each refused address a previous attempt, the TCP handshake the time `connect()` took (one round trip, also the path's RTT), TLS its handshake time; byte counts are the app's bytes (transport counts equal them), packet counts the sends and reads made, duplicates / reordering / retransmissions 0, no radio type. Tested (HelloConnections `reports`, `structured integers`, tests/ui/test_connections.py) |

Tested (swift-network `nwAPIChecks`, `nwConnectionGroupChecks`) |
| Network's C API (`nw_endpoint_*`, `nw_parameters_*` with `NW_PARAMETERS_DEFAULT_CONFIGURATION` / `NW_PARAMETERS_DISABLE_PROTOCOL`, TCP/UDP options, `nw_connection_*` with `dispatch_data_t` send/receive and content contexts (`NW_CONNECTION_*_CONTEXT`, `NW_CONNECTION_SEND_IDEMPOTENT_CONTENT`), `nw_error_*`, `nw_listener_*` with Bonjour advertising (`nw_advertise_descriptor_*`), `nw_browser_*` / `nw_browse_descriptor_*` / `nw_browse_result_*`, `nw_path_monitor_*`, `nw_retain` / `nw_release`) from C, Objective-C and Swift | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the functions forward to isim's `NWConnection`, `NWListener`, `NWBrowser` and `NWPathMonitor` (so the same sockets, OpenSSL TLS and Bonjour); the objects are Objective-C objects (ARC retains them), handlers run in order on the queue set with `nw_*_set_queue`, and a connection or listener with a state handler stays alive until it is cancelled, as on Apple platforms. Swift sees them as Apple's module does (`OS_nw_*` protocols, `nw_*_t`, the C enums as structs); there the queue setters take a `DispatchQueue` and `dispatch_data_t` is isim's C type (isim's Dispatch has no `__DispatchData`). Not yet from C: `sec_protocol_options` (TLS checks the host's CA store and the host name), protocol stacks and metadata, framers, WebSocket options, TXT record objects, connection groups, ethernet channels, data transfer reports. Tested (HelloSystemObjC: a Bonjour-advertised echo listener, a browser that finds it, a connection that echoes, TLS failing against the plain server, tests/ui/test_system_objc.py; HelloConnections from Swift, tests/ui/test_connections.py) |

| The iOS 26 Swift API: `NetworkConnection` / `NetworkChannel` (`start()`, `state`, `onStateUpdate`, `onPathUpdate`, `onViabilityUpdate`, `onBetterPathUpdate`, endpoints, `currentPath`; `send` / `receive(exactly:)` / `receive(atLeast:atMost:)` on streams, `send` / `receive()` on datagrams, WebSocket text, binary, `ping`, `pong`, `close`, TLV `send(_:type:)`, Coder `send(_:)`, `messages`), `withNetworkConnection(to:using:_:)`, `NetworkListener` (`run`, `port`, `service`, `newConnectionLimit`, state and service registration updates), `NetworkBrowser` (`run` with `RunResult`), `ListenerProvider.bonjour` / `BonjourListenerProvider`, `BrowserProvider.bonjour` / `Bonjour.Endpoint`, `Connectable`; the stack builders `IP`, `TCP`, `UDP`, `TLS` (ALPN, versions, local identity, `certificateValidator`), `WebSocket`, `TLV`, `Coder` (`NetworkCoder` `.json`, `.propertyList`), `NWParametersBuilder` and the `NWParametersProvider` modifiers, `NetworkProtocolOptions` and its marker protocols, `UnexpectedEndpointType` | ✅ | 26.0 | adapted: over isim's `NWConnection`, `NWListener` and `NWBrowser` (host sockets, OpenSSL, isim's Bonjour registry). TLV puts a big-endian type and length (UInt32 each by default) before the value; Coder frames each message with a 4-byte length on streams (one datagram per message on UDP), so isim peers interoperate with each other. A refused connection waits (`.waiting`), as `NWConnection` does, until it is ready or its task is cancelled. `NWParametersBuilder` takes one protocol stack (Apple's variadic form crashes isim's Swift 6.2 compiler). Also: `DTLS` stacks (iOS 27), `Framer` stacks (the app's framer as the one message protocol of the connection), `receive(as:)` / `send` of network-order integers, WebSocket `startSend` / `startReceive` (messages in pieces), the TLS cipher-suite modifiers and `IP.localAddressPreference`. Not on isim: QUIC streams and datagrams (isim's QUIC is a stub), Wi-Fi Aware, Apple's variadic `ProtocolStackBuilder.buildBlock(_:_:)`. Tested (HelloConnections `-structured`, tests/ui/test_connections.py `test_connections_structured`, `os_matrix`) |
| Wi-Fi Aware (`NWParameters.wifiAware`, `NWEndpoint.wifiAware`, `NWPath.wifiAware`, `NetworkConnection.wifiAware`, `BrowserProvider` / `ListenerProvider.wifiAware`, `kNWErrorDomainWiFiAware` aside) | ❌ | 26.0 | not implemented: these use the WiFiAware framework's types (`WAParameters`, `WAEndpoint`, `WAPath`, `WAConnection`), which isim does not have yet |
